after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
proposal.description: The soft-start trip is gated by a registered copy of ss_active (the state from the previous clock) instead of the live ss_active, so the gate stays open for one clock after S_SS is left.
proposal.reason: When S_SS is left, for a hiccup after a soft-start trip or for S_RUN with fault_count_ss at or above trip_ss, window_trip_SS stays high for one clock in the new state. The header forbids exactly this, because the soft-start count is frozen through S_RUN.

after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
proposal.description: The S_RUN trip is gated by a registered copy of run_active instead of the live run_active, so the gate opens one clock late and closes one clock late.
proposal.reason: After a run-window trip sends the FSM to hiccup, the run count takes one edge to clear, so window_trip stays high for the first hiccup clock. Also, a trip_run of 0 does not assert window_trip on the first clock of S_RUN.

after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
proposal.description: The S_RUN trip is made sticky: once window_trip fires it is latched until run_active falls, instead of following the run count against trip_run.
proposal.reason: Say run_active stays high after a trip, and then the run count falls below trip_run as clean cycles age faulted ones out, or trip_run is raised. window_trip should drop but stays asserted.

after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
proposal.description: The S_RUN threshold is captured on entry to S_RUN and held for the run, instead of trip_run being compared live.
proposal.reason: If trip_run changes while in S_RUN (for example it is lowered to or below the present run count), window_trip keeps using the value from before S_RUN was entered. It fails to assert, or asserts against the stale threshold.
